articles.title: Contratan a un comentarista y le despiden horas después por unos mensajes en redes... de hace 14 años
articles.standfirst: Los Blazers alegan que el implicado publicó tuits "racistas y sexistas" en 2012, cuando estaba en el instituto
articles.summary: Los Blazers alegan que el implicado publicó tuits "racistas y sexistas" en 2012, cuando estaba en el instituto
articles.body: En la mañana de este jueves, los Blazers anunciaron la contratación de Braiden Bell como nuevo comentarista. Pocas horas después era despedido. La razón: unos mensajes racistas y sexistas que publicó en sus redes sociales... hace 13 años. Bell había trabajado durante dos temporadas con las Phoenix Mercury de la WNBA y había desempeñado otros cargos en el ámbito universitario. La franquicia de Portland le contrató pensando, según palabras de su presidente de operaciones comerciales, que era "la persona ideal para la dirección que estamos tomando y una voz importante para el próximo capítulo del baloncesto de los Trail Blazers". Sin embargo, a las pocas horas, la entidad emitió un comunicado anunciando el despido del trabajador más efímero en la historia del equipo. En el escrito se decía que los Blazers no podían tolerar "comentarios racistas, sexistas o dañinos", que Bell no formaría parte de la franquicia y pedían disculpas a sus aficionados. Los mensajes en cuestión son tuits de 2012 y 2013, cuando el protagonista aún estaba en el instituto. Entre otras frases se podían leer: "Los asiáticos me sacan de quicio" y "Tenemos una alerta de zorra en el pasillo 10". Bell iba a sustituir a un ilustre comentarista de los Blazers que había dejado su puesto, según él, después de haber recibido una irrisoria oferta para firmar un nuevo contrato. Es la enésima polémica que vive la franquicia con miembros de su personal desde que llegara el propietario Tom Dundon, que ya se ha ganado fama de tacaño en el universo NBA. Nada más asumir la propiedad de la franquicia despidió a cerca de 70 empleados, entre ellos a una cuarta parte de su personal de oficinas y negocio. Para ahorrar costes, a los jugadores con contrato dual se les prohibió viajar con el equipo en playoffs y también a parte del departamento de prensa y en los hoteles se acabó el privilegio de extender la hora del checkout. Para el entrenador, el presupuesto fijado era de sólo un millón de euros, lo que hizo que Tiago Splitter no aceptara la oferta y llegara Micah Nori.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark's Full Box Score Stats, Top Higlights from 1st Round of WNBA Playoffs
articles.summary: The Indiana Fever are out of the 2026 WNBA Playoffs after failing to build on Caitlin Clark's season-saving Game 2 performance.
articles.body:
The Indiana Fever are out of the 2026 WNBA Playoffs after failing to build on Caitlin Clark's season-saving Game 2 performance.

Clark scored 18 points and added four assists Thursday night as the Fever conceded a 94-83 elimination loss to the Las Vegas Aces in Game 3 of the first round.

Here's a look at Clark's overall stats and top highlights from the Fever's three-game playoff run.

Clark went just 3-for-10 from deep as she was held to 15 points to open the series.

She still started out the series strong by making a few early three-pointers and splitting Aces defenders for a pass to Kelsey Mitchell while the Fever were still in contention early in the game.

Overall, the Fever struggled in Game 1 to contain the Aces, who shot 47.4 percent from behind the arc and converted 75 percent of their opportunities at the rim.

Clark made history while keeping the Fever's postseason hopes alive in Game 2.

She became the first player to record a points/assists double-double in one half of a playoff game by racking up 14 points and 11 assists through two quarters for the Fever.

Clark carried that momentum into the second half, finishing the game with a team-high 27 points to go along with 15 assists and seven rebounds.

She closed out the victory as the first player in WNBA history to record 25 points and 15 assists in a single playoff game.

The Fever successfully shut down Wilson in the final quarter of Game 2 to close out the win.

The Fever were unable to continue holding Wilson back with their season on the line.

Clark started out hot with 11 points in the first quarter to help the Fever stay even with the Aces.

She was held to just seven points in the remaining three quarters of play as Wilson racked up a game-high 36 points.

Clark also took an inadvertent elbow to the face in the fourth quarter during a play on which no foul was called.

This marks the second straight season in which Las Vegas has ended Indiana's title hopes. The Fever made it to the WNBA semifinals last season despite missing Clark to injury before losing to the Aces.

Clark finished her third WNBA regular season having averaged a career-high 22.3 points per game along with four rebounds, 8.3 assists and 1.1 steals per game. She told reporters after the Fever's elimination loss she considers this the best season of her career so far.

The Miami Heat announced Friday that they will hold a special promotional night on Nov. 18 in celebration of the release of the highly anticipated Grand Theft Auto VI video game on Nov. 19.

Entitled "A Night in Vice City," the promotion will see the Heat refer to themselves as Vice City rather than Miami for one night only when they host the Milwaukee Bucks.

The Heat will also wear brand-new uniforms and play on a never-before-seen court design.

Adding to the importance of the night is the fact that it will mark the first time Giannis Antetokounmpo plays against his old team since getting traded from the Bucks to the Heat during the offseason.

articles.title: Ja Morant, Damian Lillard Potentially Being Used in Bench Role Discussed by HC Ahead of NBA Season
articles.summary: With Damian Lillard set to return from injury and Ja Morant being added to the mix following an offseason trade, the Portland Trail Blazers' starting backcourt going into the 2026-27 NBA season is still being decided upon.
articles.body:
With Damian Lillard set to return from injury and Ja Morant being added to the mix following an offseason trade, the Portland Trail Blazers' starting backcourt going into the 2026-27 NBA season is still being decided upon.

Blazers head coach Micah Nori told The Athletic's Jason Quick he plans to use the preseason to tinker with the starting lineup before deciding if either Lillard or Morant will come off the bench when the regular season tips off.

Ranking Every NBA Team's Starting Lineup Ahead of Preseason 🔢

"It's not set in stone, but probably, because I'm leaning toward wanting to see what it looks like," Nori said. "And … I don't want to start a fire before I need to."

Nori's comments come after Lillard told reporters on Tuesday "as far as I know" he, Morant and Deni Avdija will all be in the starting lineup.

Lillard also said he hadn't discussed the starting five with Nori thus far. The Blazers also have Jrue Holiday as another point guard option on the roster.

According to Quick, Nori pointed out that starting Morant and Lillard "doesn't make sense" given how limited both players are defensively, which could make Holiday a more appealing option for the opening lineup.

Portland's acquisition of Morant was regarded with some confusion because of the presence of Lillard and Holiday.

B/R's Dan Favale gave the Blazers' side of the deal a "D" grade due to a combination of the players already on the team and Morant's style of play not being "particularly adaptable."

The cost to acquire Morant was so low for Portland — it only cost Jerami Grant and Kris Murray with no draft picks going back to the Memphis Grizzlies — that there's no significant risk beyond the roughly $87 million Morant is owed over the next two seasons.

Morant also offers some flexibility if Lillard is limited early in the season as he works his way back from a torn Achilles suffered on April 27, 2025. Lillard's shooting touch in practice looks to be just fine , but we have yet to see how it will play in actual games.

Our first look at the second Lillard run in Portland could come as early as Oct. 7 when the team opens preseason play against the Golden State Warriors.

articles.title: New Jalen Duren Rumors on Message from Pistons Governor That Helped Seal $200M Contract
articles.summary: Detroit Pistons owner Tom Gores reportedly played a significant role in convincing Jalen Duren to end his contract standoff by signing a five-year, $200 million deal, according to The Athletic's Sam Amick.
articles.body:
Detroit Pistons owner Tom Gores reportedly played a significant role in convincing Jalen Duren to end his contract standoff by signing a five-year, $200 million deal, according to The Athletic's Sam Amick .

According to Amick, Gores "spent Duren's decision day sending a meaningful message that played a pivotal part in his decision."

Amick reported Gores "made a promise to Duren and his family that he would help provide a more positive Pistons experience" that served as "at minimum, an acknowledgement that this sensitive situation had gone sideways."

Duren, who hit restricted free agency after averaging 19.5 points and 10.5 rebounds per game in his All-Star fourth season before his production dropped in the playoffs, was eligible for a $287 million maximum contract.

Amick first reported in June Duren was considering seeking a sign-and-trade away from Detroit after being "underwhelmed" by the Pistons' first offer.

Most of the negotiations since then apparently weren't conducted directly with Pistons president of basketball operations Trajan Langdon, who said earlier this week he had "not spoken to [Duren] all summer."

The Pistons also caused friction with Duren by including mandatory monthly weight check-ins in their initial version of the $200 million offer before rescinding the clause earlier this week, Hunter Patterson and Amick reported for The Athletic.

At least some of those issues were seemingly resolved just before the restricted free agent signing deadline of Thursday night, at which point the Pistons had increased their offer from $170 to $190 million to a fully-guaranteed $200 million, per ESPN's Shams Charania .

The Pistons will now hope to bring Duren, who missed the beginning of training camp, back into the fold before tipping off the regular season Oct. 20 against the visiting Boston Celtics.

articles.title: Aces' fans spew unfounded claims that Fever fans are 'racist' while defending A'ja Wilson
articles.summary: Las Vegas Aces fans accused Indiana Fever supporters of racism and slurs at Gainbridge Fieldhouse, but their claims crumbled under scrutiny.
articles.body: There's a glaring problem in the WNBA. From media, to the players, and the league's dedicated fan base full of left-wing political activists, far too many people have been unfairly characterizing Indiana Fever and Caitlin Clark fans. Since Clark's rookie season, the claims of racism have been leveled at an astounding rate. My conversations with Las Vegas Aces' fans proved just how hostile and unfair, to say the least, that rhetoric has become. When controversies arise in the WNBA, and across sports in general, I want to do my due diligence by asking fans what they think in person. I want to hear the thoughts and opinions from people who are invested and aware in what is going on, whether they are left, right, or center. I've done that at the Sophie Cunningham rallies and protests outside arenas across the country. I've interviewed fans in the aftermath of flagrant fouls on Caitlin Clark and Cunningham. I've covered a lot of the issues the league has faced and brought upon themselves. As you know, the WNBA is no stranger to controversies. It's engrained in the fabric of the league. So when A'ja Wilson walked over 20 feet away into the seating area during Game 2 to confront a fan in Indiana for simply pointing at her from the second row of the baseline courtside seats, I wanted to hear fans thoughts about it. I wanted their thoughts on the WNBA refusing to reprimand the league's MVP or have Wilson face any repercussions whatsoever for her actions. Those questions triggered some insane accusations from Aces fans regarding the Fever fan and their fanbase. PRIME VIDEO WNBA BROADCAST CREW EMBARRASSES ITSELF WITH COVERAGE OF A'JA WILSON FAN INCIDENT About an hour before gametime, I spoke with a female Aces fan, who said, "I think it (the A'ja Wilson incident) is bigger than that moment. I think it's more about racism and the concerns regarding the Fever fans being racist." That's the way this incident was framed from the beginning, unfortunately. It was a Black athlete confronting a White fan, so people jumped at the idea there must have been a slur thrown in Wilson's direction. That was obviously not the case.She then continued by disagreeing with A'ja Wilson's actions, but justified them due to claims of racism: "She was out of line to approach a fan like that, but by the same token, racism in our country is also out of line." When I asked if she thought the fan was racist she responded, "No. Not at all." I was now a little confused, so I asked if she was claiming the fan wasn't racist, but that race played a factor in A'ja Wilson losing her cool. "I do," she said definitively. "I think as a Black athlete, in a state where there's a history of racism, and where this team has been accused of having racist fans," she continued before I cut her off to ask if there's validity to those claims. "I think there's validity to racism," she responded. "Well, of course, but [I'm asking about] Indiana Fever fans," I responded. FORMER ESPN ANCHOR SMEARS CAITLIN CLARK FANS WITH SWEEPING, FALSE ACCUSATIONS OF RACISM | MATT CALKINS "No, I can't say that," she humbly responded, realizing she was assigning labels to a fanbase without proper proof. The conversation went on for another minute or so where I respectfully pressed her on her characterization of the Fever fan base and how they've been labeled as racists, bigots, you name it. I even mentioned that Wilson even stated in the postgame interview that her actions weren't because of anything he said, but the fact that a man pointed at her. If anything, she was claiming some form of misogyny. The fan still speculated that race could've played a part in Wilson's thinking, leading her to lose her cool. In another conversation, an Aces fan unashamedly said that she believes Indiana Fever fans are "racist." She claimed, "It's (Gainbridge Fieldhouse) a hard place and the way they treat us up there. I've sat there and watched games and watched them yell slurs." When I asked her if she believed a slur was said by the fan towards Wilson, knowing good and well that no slur was stated because both I and Pat McAfee Show personality, Boston Connor, who was seated by the fan, have confirmed the fan simply said, "It (the foul) is on you," she responded by saying, "It's kinda hard to say. He did something to provoke her because that's not A'ja and that's not her demeanor." This is where I let her know that multiple sources have confirmed nothing racial was said to Wilson. "But then, the way he came [at her], he left his seat, he left his area, and he stepped towards her," she responded trying to find a way to justify Wilson's unsportsmanlike actions, though she was just proven to be ignorant about the facts. She continued by saying the Fever fan was "provoking" Wilson and seemingly questioned his intentions as a threat to Wilson's safety. Here's where things went completely off the rails. LET'S HAVE AN HONEST CONVERSATION ABOUT CAITLIN CLARK, RACISM, AND MEDIA COWARDICE| BOBBY BURACK She then claimed the WNBA made the right decision to not eject, fine, or suspend Wilson, because Indiana Fever fans are "racists." I'm not kidding. This was actually her argument. "If you've never been to Cambridge Fieldhouse and seen the demeanor of the Indiana Fever fans," she mistakenly said while referring to Gainbridge Fieldhouse. "If we did half of what they did up there, the WNBA would be fining the Aces." So now was the time to get the clarification we are all looking for. I asked, "Do you believe Indiana Fever fans are racist?" She responded with a resounding, "Yes! By all means! By all means! By all means! Yes, they are racists." So here is the problem. Fans like this, making outlandish claims that aren't based in facts or reality, are what is wrong with the WNBA. They spew unfounded talking points about Fever fans. It's been that way since Clark entered the league three seasons ago. The millions of people who have flocked to the league because of Caitlin Clark, helping players like A'ja Wilson sign million dollar contracts, assisted in teams now flying private, and who may be the fans who help make the league profitable for the first time in the league's 30-year history, are labeled as the scum of the earth. They might as well be considered the KKK of WNBA fanbases. An insane, divisive, unfair label that echoes the claims of even A'ja Wilson's mom, who paraded around the arena with a "Love Beats Hate" sign following the Aces' Game 3 win. articles.title: NBA reportedly won't discipline Wizards, Bub Carrington after guard admitted team held back to get AJ Dybantsa
articles.summary: The Wizards recorded only 17 victories in 2025-26 — their second-fewest in single-season franchise history — before winning the No. 1 overall pick and drafti...
articles.body:
The NBA cracked down on purposeful losing, otherwise known as "tanking," last season. Back in February, the league fined the Utah Jazz $500,000 and the Indiana Pacers $100,000 for fishy roster-management behavior that NBA commissioner Adam Silver described as "overt" in its prioritization of draft position over winning.

Then, in May, the league announced its new anti-tanking rules , which will be in place for at least the 2027-29 drafts. The draft lottery will grow from 14 to 16 teams. Lottery odds will be flattened further. And, most notably, the teams with the three worst records will be penalized .

But as much as the NBA is trying to eliminate tanking, it's reportedly letting an admission of the integrity-threatening practice slide ahead of the 2026-27 campaign. Washington Wizards guard Bub Carrington, a 21-year-old gearing up for his third season with the organization, confessed that the Wizards didn't give their all last season. Yet, according to a Friday report from The Athletic's Sam Amick , the NBA won't discipline Washington or Carrington.

"We just haven't been told yet to go be the best version of yourself," Carrington said in a now-viral clip from a 1-on-1 interview with Washington TV station WUSA9.

Carrington was asked to clarify what he meant.

"We've all, in a way, been held back. Just because … we were trying to get AJ Dybantsa."

Carrington continued before letting out a laugh: "That's no secret."

He repeated those three words again before adding, "But now, no one has handcuffs. Everyone's shackles-free. So that alone is already a conversation starter. But then you put that on top of the coaching, on top of the vets that we have — that's a playoff team.

"And that's gonna happen. … And then when it does happen, it'll happen for a long time."

Really, what's been a conversation starter is Carrington's candor. His remarks were only surprising because he actually said what everyone was thinking.

The Wizards recorded only 17 victories in 2025-26 — their second-fewest in single-season franchise history — before winning the No. 1 overall pick and drafting Dybantsa.

They were among a handful of teams, a group that included the Jazz and the Pacers, not so discretely jockeying for draft positioning last season, after which a talent-laden class of NBA prospects were available for the taking.

Dybantsa, a standout forward who averaged a nation-leading 25.5 points in his lone season at BYU, headlined that cohort.

The Wizards, who haven't won more than 18 games in each of the past three go-arounds, traded for four-time All-Star guard Trae Young and 10-time All-Star big man Anthony Davis during last season. But Washington didn't hurry them back from the injuries they had suffered with the Atlanta Hawks and Dallas Mavericks, respectively. Young wound up appearing in only five games with the Wizards, and Davis has yet to play in a contest with Washington.

Not only that, but the Wizards gave plenty of minutes to players who had spent time with their G League team, including those on two-way contracts.

With Young and Davis in the rotation, plus a young corps surrounding them, the Wizards could be one of the most improved teams in the NBA this season. They also might be one of the last beneficiaries of tanking as we knew it.

articles.title: Un sólido Barça muestra su poderío ante un Besiktas caótico
articles.standfirst: Punter (16) y Gibson (15) comandan el convincente triunfo azulgrana en Estambul
articles.summary: Punter (16) y Gibson (15) comandan el convincente triunfo azulgrana en Estambul
articles.body: Un Barça tremendamente sólido, aguerrido en defensa y muy acertado desde el triple (9/21) desarboló con relativa facilidad a un Besiktas caótico y demasiado individualista (82-95). La gran defensa azulgrana sumió a los turcos en un desorden y una inoperancia preocupantes que les llevó a jugarse la baza de los triples en vano (8/33). Punter (16) y Gibson (15) fueron los mejores de los de Sekulic. Mientras que Wilbekin (17) y Zizic (10+9) destacaron entre los locales, que evitaron una paliza mayor gracias a sus 18 rebotes ofensivos, el único lunar culé en Estambul. Dotson lideró las primeras embestidas del Besiktas (6-2), una efervescencia que fue diluida pronto por la eficaz telaraña defensiva de un Barça muy proactivo que con un parcial de 2-18 fabricado con puntos de ocho jugadores diferentes y coronado con triples de Umude y Martin puso la máxima en el marcador (8-20, min 8). Wilbekin, con cinco puntos, comandó la reacción de los turcos, muy erráticos en los tiros (3/13 t2 y 2/9 t3), pero que sacaban petróleo de sus siete rebotes ofensivos (17-25, min 10). El resurgimiento del Besiktas continuó al inico del segundo acto con Wilbekin, Dotson y Gabriel completando un parcial de 14-5 (24-27, min 14). No hubo sorpasso porque los azulgranas cortaron esa inercia con los triples de Minaya, Punter y Brizuela que devolvieron la máxima a los suyos (31-43, min 16). Brown y Nowell frenaron la sangría, aunque Brizuela, Parra y Gibson continuaron percutiendo en el aro turco para mantener la renta al descanso (40-52, min 20). No cejó el Barça en su empeño de estiran su ventaja y en la reanudación lo hizo con autoridad gracias a Balcerowski, Gibson y Nkamohua, que pusieron una nueva máxima (49-63, min 25). Los turcos, muy individualistas, se estrellaban una y otra vez contra el muro defensivo azulgrana y en defensa eran taladrados por sus tiradores. Wilbekin y Zizic les sacaron por momentos de la UVI, a la que regresaron heridos por el acierto de Robinson, Martin, Umude y Gibson (62-77, min 30). articles.title: Giannis Predicts Heat Will Be 'Nightmare' Defensively for Opponents During 2026-27 NBA Season
articles.summary: Miami Heat forward Giannis Antetokounmpo believes his new team's defense will be a "nightmare" for opponents to attack this season, per comments made to ESPN's Hannah Storm in a preseason interview alongside center Bam Adebayo.
articles.body:
Miami Heat forward Giannis Antetokounmpo believes his new team's defense will be a "nightmare" for opponents to attack this season, per comments made to ESPN's Hannah Storm in a preseason interview alongside center Bam Adebayo.

"I think defensively it's gonna be a nightmare for whoever try to play against us," Antetokounmpo said .

Adebayo also noted how teams might have problems on both ends of the court.

Antetokounmpo played his first 13 seasons with the Milwaukee Bucks. He is a 10-time All-Star, a nine-time All-NBA player and two-time regular season MVP. Antetokounmpo also led the 2020-21 Bucks to an NBA championship capped by his 50-point performance in Game 6 of the NBA Finals en route to NBA Finals MVP honors.

After nearly a decade-and-a-half in Milwaukee, Antetokounmpo was ready for a new challenge and desired a move to a team closer to a championship. He found one in the Miami Heat, who acquired him and Bobby Portis in a blockbuster deal.

Now Antetokounmpo is teaming up with Adebayo, an amazing player in his own right at the peak of his career. Adebayo is a three-time All-Star and six-time All-NBA Defensive Team member who is a significant matchup problem on both ends.

The duo can certainly lead Miami to greater heights after last season ended in a play-in tournament loss.

Otherwise, Antetokounmpo seems to be enjoying the warmer weather .

"It's been fun," Antetokounmpo said. "I'm enjoying the warm weather. It's good for my knees and back and my joints. It's a big change for me but change is good. I've been having fun."

Miami has a good challenge early when the team hosts the Minnesota Timberwolves on Wednesday, Oct. 21.

articles.title: El Valencia Basket sigue invicto tras levantar 18 puntos con un Mirotic para la historia

articles.summary: Los taronjas sobreviven al aluvión de triples del ASVEL y remontan con una gran segunda parte en la que destacó el ala-pívot: 22 puntos y tercer máximo anotador histórico de la Euroliga
articles.body: De ser arrollado, a arrollar. El Valencia Basket sumó la tercera victoria y se mantiene invicto en este inicio de la Euroliga después de derrotar al ASVEL Villeurbanne por 92-105. Un gran inicio del primer proyecto de Xavi Albert. Con la misma filosofía que la temporada pasada, con marcadores abultados y sabiendo sufrir, pues se encontró 18 puntos abajo (60-42), está ahí en lo alto. Al ritmo de TJ Shorts (17 puntos y seis asistencias), con un Taylor decisivo en el tramo final (14) y un Mirotic para la historia, los taronjas sacaron una victoria que se había puesto casi imposible. El ala-pívot fue el mejor anotador de su equipo con 22 puntos en algo menos de 18 minutos. Físicamente quizás no esté para proezas, pero su calidad sigue intacta. Listo para seguir agrandando su leyenda en la Euroliga. Durante el choque superó a Vassilis Spanoulis en la lista de máximos anotadores históricos de la competición. Es tercero. El Valencia padeció un aluvión de triples (10/15) que llevó a los galos a batir su tope anotador en una mitad en la máxima competición europea: 61-50. Patty Mills, a sus 38 años, dio un recital. Llegó al intermedio con 17 puntos, 4/4 en triples y un solo fallo en el tiro. Acabó con 26 sin volver a acertar desde fuera. Besson era su mejor escudero (19). De la defensa taronja, sobre todo de la exterior, no había noticias. Y en ataque, los tres triples de Puerto en el primer cuarto habían sido lo mejor. Pero, tras el descanso, todo cambió. Los taronjas salieron del vestuario con mucha más intensidad, a los locales se les cerró el grifo (3/16 desde el arco en la segunda mitad) y, con el tridente TJ Shorts-Taylor-Mirotic, no sólo le dieron a vuelta al marcador sino que se acabaron llevando una victoria holgada. El parcial de 1-8 con el que se cerró la primera mitad (61-50) fue un anticipo de lo que vendría después. Un 3-15 en la reanudación para ponerse por delante (64-65). Shorts y Mirotic tiraron del conjunto valenciano y aguantaron los intentos del ASVEL por levantarse. Llovía mucho menos. Ahora sí tenía una defensa enfrente. Metió sólo 16 puntos en el tercer periodo y 31 en toda la segunda parte. En el último acto, Mirotic volvió a tomar la iniciativa en ataque mientras Sako se pegaba bajo los aros. Mills estaba fallón y, con ello, los franceses casi no amenazaban. La puntilla la dio Taylor con siete puntos seguidos: 89-98 a falta de 1:24. Tras aquel -18, la respuesta taronja fue un 32-63. articles.title: Baskonia reina en la locura del Buesa y se lleva el primer triunfo en Euroliga

articles.summary: El equipo de Galbiati consigue una trabajada victoria ante Armani Milán en un partido que lideró de inicio a fin pero que necesitó pelear por los múltiples parciales de ambos equipos
articles.body: Baskonia consiguió la primera victoria de la temporada (86-76) en un sufrido y trabajado partido que dominó de principio a fin pero que no pudo cerrar hasta los últimos minutos. Un gran inicio de primer cuarto (15-4) allanó el camino para dominar el encuentro, pero Armani Milán no se iba a rendir tan fácilmente. Gracias a un brillante Devon Hall, los italianos se aferraban al marcador y amenazaron con llevarse el partido en el último periodo, pero los triples de Lawson y Stewart, el descaro de Duarte y la garra del debutante Santos permitieron al Buesa Arena celebrar el primer triunfo en Euroliga de la temporada. El equipo de Paolo Galbiati salió enchufado desde el primer momento (8-0) y colocó una distancia en el marcador que mantuvo durante todo el primer cuarto. En un primer tramo en el que aportaron todos los titulares, Baskonia se marchó 10 puntos arriba (26-16) con cuatro triples anotados, liderados por un inspirado A.J. Lawson. El equipo vitoriano mantuvo esas diferencias durante los siguientes diez minutos, incluso amenazando con estirar esa renta máxima y poder romper el partido ante un Armani Milán que era incapaz de meter un triple (0/10 a falta de 14 segundos para el descanso). Sin embargo, un buen último minuto y el primer acierto desde el 6,75 por parte de Ricci dejaron a los italianos a ocho puntos. Tras el paso por vestuarios, comenzó la locura de parciales en ambos equipos. Un excelso Devon Hall llevaba a los suyos a dos puntos en sólo dos minutos (2-11 en 2:05), pero el arreón de Chris Duarte y Marcio Santos volvieron a colocar a Baskonia once puntos arriba a falta de un minuto. El pívot brasileño dejó una buena carta de presentación con 10 puntos y 6 rebotes. Armani Milán se acercaba poco a poco en el marcador mientras Hall lograba a falta de nueve minutos el doble doble. Amenazaron tanto los italianos que un 3-12 de salida puso por delante a los italianos (70-72 a falta de 6:43). No obstante, en el peor momento para Baskonia, reaccionó de la mejor manera posible. El dominicano y el brasileño volvieron a levantar a la grada, acompañados por un Baugh acertado para poner el 78-72 a falta de 3:22 para la bocina. El Buesa apretó en los minutos finales y dos triples de Baugh y Kurucs sellaron la primera victoria (87-76) para Baskonia en Euroliga, importante para Baskonia en el primero de los tres compromisos que tiene consecutivos en casa. articles.title: Craig Carton calls out cancel culture after Portland Trail Blazers cut ties with newly hired announcer
articles.summary: Craig Carton ripped the Portland Trail Blazers for firing Braiden Bell over old tweets, arguing a 14-year-old's posts shouldn't cost a dream job.
articles.body: By now, I'm sure you're all aware of the situation regarding the Portland Trail Blazers firing their newly hired play-by-play announcer. It's a tale as old as time: someone lands their dream job, then an amateur internet sleuth with nothing better to do takes it upon themselves to ruin their life by digging up insensitive social media posts from over a decade ago. Many sane people thought we had made it to the other side of "cancel culture," but apparently that isn't the case. MICHAEL RAPAPORT TELLS CRAIG CARTON THAT HIS SUPPORT FOR ISRAEL HAS COST HIM WORK IN HOLLYWOOD Braiden Bell was all set to be the newest play-by-play guy for the Blazers, until a man by the name of Devon Haskins of KGW News in Portland unearthed several "racist and misogynist" tweets belonging to Bell from 2012 and 2013. The tweets are, admittedly, in poor taste, but, to be fair, Bell was 14 years old at the time. CRAIG CARTON CALLS OUT PABLO TORRE FOR TYING TIM TEBOW TO ALLEGED LIFE SURGE SCAM: 'SHAME ON YOU' OutKick's Craig Carton weighed in on the situation, and was pretty charged up about what went down. "This kid just got the job of his lifetime," an incensed Carton explains. "And the first thing an 'investigative reporter' wants to do is see if (he) can find some dirt on the kid." While he isn't condoning what Bell posted, Carton is quick to point out that he was a teenager when he wrote this stuff, and that pretty much everyone has said something dumb or insensitive in their younger years. "I'm not excusing what he wrote. I understand you finding it offensive, but he didn't write it as a mature adult," Carton says. FIERY VIEWS ON LINDSAY CLANCY AT WORK COULD GET YOU FIRED — AND BE PERFECTLY LEGAL, EMPLOYMENT LAWYER WARNS "He wrote it as a 14 year old. Are we really going to make decisions now and not allowing people to get jobs? Because when they were in high school, they put out a tweet that their friends might have found funny, and now it's going to impact this guy for the rest of his life." Carton is spot on. UNIVERSITY PAYS PROFESSOR $600K AFTER BEING PUNISHED FOR PARODYING LAND ACKNOWLEDGMENTS What does a guy like Haskins gain from digging up these Tweets from half a lifetime ago. The only thing that comes of this is that some poor young man was robbed of his dream job for the (admittedly forgivable) sins he committed as a teenager. As a media man himself, Carton has one key piece of advice for anyone looking to make it big in broadcasting: scrub your social media page NOW. "Before you apply for a job... clean out the Twitter account, clean out the Instagram," he pleads. "Because you don't even remember the dumb s–t you said and posted when you were a child." articles.title: Steve Kerr Addresses Stephen Curry's 'Rare' Contract Paycut, Emphasizes Cap Space Flexibility
articles.summary: Golden State Warriors head coach Steve Kerr spoke with ESPN's Anthony Slater on Friday from Oahu, Hawaii, where the team is holding its training camp on the BYU-Hawaii campus.
articles.body:
Golden State Warriors head coach Steve Kerr spoke with ESPN's Anthony Slater on Friday from Oahu, Hawaii, where the team is holding its training camp on the BYU-Hawaii campus.

During the talk, Kerr was asked about Curry's new two-year, $116 million deal , which is more than $20 million less than the maximum he was eligible to sign. Slater referenced pay cuts that Hall of Famer, ex-San Antonio Spurs star and Kerr's former teammate, Tim Duncan, late in his career.

NBA Players with the All-Time Most Career Earnings💰

"Yeah, Timmy did that a couple of different times late in his career," Kerr began. "Manu Ginobili did it. It's something that is very rare, but if it happens, it usually happens with a person like Steph or Tim Duncan and someone who is with one organization their entire career, where it's just a relationship that allows for it. So it didn't surprise anyone. Steph is obviously still making a ton of money, but he's very unselfish and understands that this pickup will allow us next summer to sign better players, more players."

Curry has played all 17 of his NBA seasons with the Warriors. He's won four NBA championships and two NBA MVP awards while making 11 All-NBA teams.

The 12-time All-Star and two-time scoring champion has averaged 24.8 points, 6.3 assists and 4.7 rebounds over his career.

He'll be a first-ballot Hall of Famer someday and can at least make a case for being the best point guard in league history, and he's considered one of the best (if not the best) shooters in NBA history.

Curry's accomplished basically all that one can at this stage of his career, and he's earned nearly half a billion dollars on his contracts, per Spotrac . Of course, chasing championships never gets old, so it makes sense that Curry took a pay cut to give Golden State more cap flexibility.

As Kerr noted, Curry is still being paid handsomely, though $20 million isn't exactly a small amount to turn down.

This year's Warriors team has the talent to compete and make the playoffs with Curry back. The key is staying healthy and hopefully an earlier-than-expected return from Jimmy Butler (torn ACL). Butler says he is ahead of schedule, but a return timeline is unclear .

Golden State is also without Kristaps Porziņģis, who is out indefinitely with an undisclosed health issue.

Still, Draymond Green, Al Horford, rookie Yaxel Lendeborg and Brandin Podziemski should help. They'll get their first test on Oct. 21 at the Los Angeles Lakers.

We believe strongly that everyone who is a part of Rip City should feel welcome and safe and we will make sure that our new broadcaster reflects these values. We will do better.

The matter of the Blazers' play-by-play announcer was already a source of some embarrassment for the team. That job was only open due to the departure of longtime broadcaster Kevin Calabro , who said he left after receiving a "subprime" offer for his new contract with the team.

The most recent developments leave the Blazers without a permanent play-by-play broadcaster with preseason set to begin Wednesday and the regular season on Oct. 21.

articles.title: Cade Tyson still awaiting Gophers eligibility as key hearing approaches
articles.summary: We might receive some clarity on Cade Tyson's eligibility soon.
articles.body:
The 2026-27 Gophers men's basketball team will play a game, albeit an exhibition, this month, and we still don't know if last season's leading scorer, Cade Tyson, will be eligible to play. An Oct. 13 hearing in federal appeals court could provide more clarity on his situation.

Tyson is among numerous athletes across the country pursuing a fifth year of eligibility after the NCAA adopted a new age-based eligibility model earlier this year. Under the new rules, athletes generally can compete during a continuous five-year eligibility period that begins with either their initial full-time college enrollment or when they turn 19.

The transition rules, however, did not grant an additional season to athletes such as Tyson who exhausted their eligibility under the previous rules during the 2025-26 academic year.

Tyson was a member of the 2022 high school recruiting class and played four seasons of college basketball. He is among the athletes arguing that they should be allowed to compete for a fifth season under the NCAA's new model.

In early July, Tyson was among a group of 12 athletes named as plaintiffs in a federal lawsuit against the NCAA in Colorado. A federal judge eventually granted a class-wide preliminary injunction in late July that prevented the NCAA from enforcing its eligibility rules against qualifying athletes from the 2022 high school class.

But the Tenth Circuit Court of Appeals later granted the NCAA's request to stay that preliminary injunction while the NCAA's appeal is pending. That means athletes whose eligibility depended solely on the Colorado injunction are once again ineligible unless they have obtained separate relief through another court.

Niko Medved and the Gophers revealed in early September that Tyson has re-enrolled in classes at the University of Minnesota and is practicing with the team, but his eligibility status remains uncertain. Roster restrictions and financial compensation concerns were cleared up, and we know that if Tyson returns to college basketball, it will be at Minnesota.

There's still a full month until Minnesota's regular-season opener on Nov. 2 against North Dakota, but there are a pair of exhibitions looming on Oct. 15 against Omaha and Oct. 23 against Creighton. It's fair to assume Minnesota would prefer some clarity on Tyson's status as it seeks to find its preferred rotation for the 2026-27 season.

The Tenth Circuit Court of Appeals in Denver is scheduled to hear arguments on Oct. 13 in Wisne v. NCAA , the case in which Tyson is a named plaintiff. Andy Greder of the Pioneer Press was the first to report the upcoming hearing as it relates to Tyson.

The hearing does not guarantee a ruling on Oct. 13, but the arguments could provide additional insight into how the appeals court views the dispute. The court is considering the NCAA's appeal of the preliminary injunction that had temporarily opened the door for Tyson and similarly situated athletes to receive another season of eligibility.

There have been numerous cases similar to Tyson's around the country, with courts reaching differing conclusions.

Most recently, on Friday, the Ohio First District Court of Appeals reversed a court's preliminary injunction that had allowed roughly two dozen Class of 2022 athletes to pursue a fifth season. A three-judge panel unanimously sided with the NCAA on the preliminary injunction, making the affected athletes ineligible again while that litigation continues.

Other athletes have successfully obtained temporary restraining orders or preliminary injunctions in separate cases, illustrating just how unsettled the eligibility issue remains.

Oct. 13 could provide more clarity on Tyson's path toward playing for the Gophers this season, but with eligibility lawsuits producing different results in courts around the country, a definitive answer may not come immediately.

articles.title: Braiden Bell ‘deeply sorry’ for old tweets that cost him Blazers announcer job
articles.summary: It stands to reason most NBA fans didn’t know who Braiden Bell was before Thursday morning, when he was announced as the new TV play-by-play voice of the Por...
articles.body:
It stands to reason most NBA fans didn't know who Braiden Bell was before Thursday morning, when he was announced as the new TV play-by-play voice of the Portland Trail Blazers.

Unfortunately, they knew his name by Thursday evening, when the NBA franchise announced it was moving on from Bell after discovering several offensive social media posts he wrote as a teenager.

"The Portland Trail Blazers have zero tolerance for racist, sexist, or harmful comments," the team said in an official statement . "Social media posts made by our recently announced play-by-play broadcaster are in clear violation of team and league policies, as well as our values and expectations. Therefore, we will not be moving forward with this broadcaster."

KGW reporter Devon Haskins first reported on Bell's offending posts , which included several misogynistic and racist tweets in 2012 and 2013, when he was a teenager.

On Friday, the 29-year-old Bell released a statement apologizing for the posts he wrote at 14, adding that they "have no reflection of who I am today."

"I regret this being the first impression to many of you online, but I can take solace in knowing that the people who truly know me understand that this is not the kind of person I am, "wrote Bell on X. "Again, I'd like to apologize to anyone who was hurt by my words and will continue to always treat people with kindness and respect."

The whiplash affair sparked intense discussions across social media about the standards people should be held to for what they said online in the past, especially before they become adults.

In what might be another example to add to that discussion, Haskins' own social media history became fodder for those looking to showcase a presumed double standard. He deleted his X account on Friday.

articles.title: Cooper Webb confirmed with Team Tedder, Husqvarna
articles.summary: Cooper Webb will debut on the Husqvarna this weekend in the Motocross of Nations.
articles.body:
Long rumored, Cooper Webb's move to Team Tedder Racing has been confirmed with an announcement that they will debut the relationship in this week's Motocross of Nations in Ernee, France. He will join Justin Hill on the team.

Husqvarna Mobility has joined Team Tedder in the newly formed partnership that will see Webb on an Austrian bike for the first time since he parted ways with Red Bull KTM midway through the 2023 Pro Motocross season.

The deal is described as a multi-year deal and will include the entire 17-round Monster Energy Supercross Championship and presumably the SuperMotocross World Championship Playoffs if Webb qualifies.

"We're really excited about what we've put together for next year," Team Manager Dakota Tedder said in a news release. "Bringing Cooper onto Rocky Mountain ATV/MC – Monster Energy – Team Tedder – Husqvarna, along with Justin Hill, and making the move to Husqvarna is a huge step for our team and family. We've been doing this a long time, and our goal has always been to keep that family feel, while continuing to grow the team and put ourselves in a position to race for wins and championships.

"Having a guy like Cooper believe in what we're building means a lot to us. He knows what he wants, he knows what it takes to win, and we've been able to put together a program around him that I think is going to be really special. Having the support of Husqvarna behind us is a huge part of that, and we're excited to get to work with everyone there. It's also pretty cool that our first race together is MXoN. For Cooper to represent Team USA and make his debut with us on the Husqvarna is an awesome way to kick things off together – we're excited to go racing."

In his final season with Monster Energy Star Racing, Webb finished third in Supercross, eighth in Pro Motocross, and fifth in SuperMotocross this year.

articles.title: Domantas Sabonis Calls Out 'Made Up' Kings Trade Rumors Ahead of 2026-27 NBA Season
articles.summary: Sacramento Kings center Domantas Sabonis explained that it wasn't difficult for him to ignore the trade rumors that surrounded him during the 2026 offseason.
articles.body:
Sacramento Kings center Domantas Sabonis explained that it wasn't difficult for him to ignore the trade rumors that surrounded him during the 2026 offseason.

"Easy. It's all made up," Sabonis told Johnny Askounis of Eurohoops (h/t Sam Amico of Hoops Wire). "I don't know where you guys get most of it from. I'm there with Scott [Perry], with my agent, so I'm not on social media as much."

On June 16, NBA insider Jake Fischer reported that the Kings and Charlotte Hornets discussed a swap involving Sabonis ahead of the 2026 draft. Fischer noted that the talks were "widely described as exploratory."

NBA Trade To Boost a New Eastern Conference Contender 🏀

Fischer and NBA insider Marc Stein also reported that Sacramento had interest in adding Detroit Pistons center Jalen Duren as part of a sign-and-trade agreement that would have sent Sabonis to Detroit on June 30.

Sabonis remains on the Kings' roster with the start of the 2026-27 regular season drawing closer, though.

He has two years left on his current contract, as he's set to earn $45.5 million for his 2026-27 campaign before receiving $48.6 million for the 2027-28 season (via Spotrac ).

Sabonis was limited to just 19 appearances last season due to a meniscus tear , averaging 15.8 points and 11.4 rebounds per game while shooting 54.3 percent from the field.

At 30 years old, Sabonis' long-term future in Sacramento is uncertain as the team looks to build around young pieces such as Darius Acuff Jr. and Maxime Raynaud moving forward.

For now, he's set to enter the 2026-27 season as the Kings' starting center.

articles.title: Stephen Curry reveals how his wife Ayesha Curry reacted to massive $20 million pay cut in Warriors contract extension
articles.summary: A $20 million pay cut is a hard thing to bring home.
articles.body: A $20 million pay cut is a hard thing to bring home. Stephen Curry took one in the Warriors extension, signing for roughly that much less than the top figure, and he had to tell his wife, Ayesha, about it.In an interview with ABC7 News Bay Area, Curry took on the idea that the decision must have been stressful. He pointed to gratitude, the odd scale of NBA money and the first contract he ever signed. Then he explained why the whole household is aligned.Stephen Curry explains how Ayesha Curry reacted to the $20 million pay cutStephen Curry told Ayesha he would be taking something of a pay cut for the rest of his time with the Warriors, and he later described how the conversation went to ABC7 News Bay Area. The interview was reported on Friday, October 2.What came through was agreement. When the talk turned to Ayesha and the rest of the family, Curry said "everybody's on the same page" about the part of the situation he can control. He did not quote her directly in the portion that has been reported.In practical terms, the pay cut means the guard accepted less than the most he could have been paid. The $20 million is the gap between that ceiling and the extension. Curry says the family sees it his way.He also shrank the question. People ask whether a decision like this stressed him out, Curry said, and his answer leaned on gratitude and understanding. The figures in the NBA, from team valuations to the salary cap to max deals, can feel unreal, he admitted. “'Oh, you stressed out about the decision,' and all that–the gratitude and understanding, the numbers we're talking about, and of course there's team valuations and the salary cap, max numbers and all,” the Warriors veteran shared.Curry started with the odd economics of the league, moved to his first contract, then to his family, and finished on the court. Each step came back to what he can control.Curry ties the Warriors extension to his first NBA contractTo explain how he thinks about money, Curry went back to the beginning. His first contract was worth $44 million, at about $11 million a season, and he said this decision traces back to it. “It goes back to my very first contract, the $11 million, the four for $44 million that I signed. You sign contracts based on information that you have and what you feel like is right.”A player signs a contract based on the information available and on what feels right at the time, he said. The instinct behind that first signing is the one he cites now. By that standard, the extension is one more call made with the facts he has.The destination is just as clear in his words. The Dream punched their ticket to the semifinals by sweeping the Washington Mystics, while the Liberty pulled off an upset victory over the top-seeded Minnesota Lynx.

New York is once again led by Breanna Stewart and Sabrina Ionescu, taking down Minnesota due to Stewart's prowess around the rim while also firing away from behind the arc.

The Liberty have attempted 28.5 three-pointers per game in the postseason, ranking No. 2 among all teams. They've also connected on 40.4 percent of their triples in the playoffs.

New York will look to keep pace with Atlanta's explosive guard duo of Allisha Gray and Rhyne Howard, who both earned their fourth All-Star nods this season.

It'll be intriguing to see how Stewart fares against a Dream frontcourt spearheaded by Angel Reese, as she was named the WNBA Defensive Player of the Year on Thursday. Atlanta's 92.1 defensive rating in the playoffs represents the No. 1 mark in the league (via WNBA.com ).

As for the Valkyries, they're looking to go on a deep playoff run and contend for a championship against an experienced Aces squad that is searching for their fourth title in five years.

articles.title: Valkyries coach Natalie Nakase reportedly 'fine' after sideline collapse during Game 3 vs. Wings
articles.summary: Nakase was in a heated discussion with an official when she fell to the floor.
articles.body:
It's unclear what happened to Golden State Valkyries head coach Natalie Nakase down the stretch of Game 3 against the Dallas Wings on Friday , but her team doesn't seem too concerned.

In the final two minutes of a 77-73 Valkyries win, Nakase was having a heated discussion with an official when she collapsed to her knees with her head to the ground. She was quickly helped to the Valkyries bench while appearing to be in discomfort.

It was a concerning incident, but Nakase remained in the game and was calling plays in the huddle seconds later.

The Valkyries told ESPN after the game that Nakase was exhausted and got light-headed during the incident, but was fine later. Valkyries star Gabby Williams also said, "We're glad she's alright."

Valkyries assistant coach Kasib Powell spoke with reporters after the game in Nakase's place and said she was "fine," in great spirits and was talking and laughing back in the locker room, per Kenzo Fukuda of ClutchPoints . Powell couldn't provide specifics beyond that, but said Nakase would be ready for Game 1 of the WNBA semifinals on Sunday.

The game will be against the Las Vegas Aces, with whom Nakase won two titles as an assistant coach under Becky Hammon.

Nakase's collapse was a small part of a historic thriller for the Valkyries, who clinched their first playoff series win in their second season of existence. The team overcame a 16-point third-quarter deficit and eked out a win with timely plays down the stretch, many of which came from Williams, who scored 17 of her team-high 19 points in the second half.

Nakase has been the Valkyries' coach for both of their seasons, earning WNBA Coach of the Year honors last season. Golden State had the league's second-best record in the regular season at 32-12.

articles.title: ‘Can’t Get Much Bigger Than This,’ ‘GOAT’s HOME’ – Sports World Buzzes as Caitlin Clark Joins College GameDay’s 1st Iowa Visit in 20 Years for Ohio State Clash
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark is heading back to Iowa City, and she is doing it for one of the biggest football weekends the Hawkeye community has seen in years. The Fever s...
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark is heading back to Iowa City, and she is doing it for one of the biggest football weekends the Hawkeye community has seen in years. The Fever star will serve as the celebrity guest picker on ESPN's College GameDay when No. 14 Iowa hosts No. 5 Ohio State on Saturday.

Clark's appearance comes days after her WNBA season ended with Indiana Fever's playoff loss to the Las Vegas Aces, giving the Iowa legend a chance to return home almost immediately. Needless to say, the CC fanbase was hyped by the news.

Caitlin Clark's College GameDay Appearance Has Iowa Fans Buzzing

ESPN's College GameDay announced Clark's appearance Friday evening, calling her a "Hawkeye legend" and confirming that she will join the crew for Saturday's broadcast in Iowa City.

As a guest picker, Clark will give her own predictions for the day's marquee matchup alongside the GameDay panel.

The show begins at 9 a.m. ET and runs until 12 p.m. ET, with the GameDay set at the Pentacrest. The football game between Iowa and Ohio State is scheduled for 3:30 p.m. ET.

Clark will join a stacked GameDay panel featuring Rece Davis, Kirk Herbstreit, Desmond Howard, Nick Saban, Pete Thamel, and Pat McAfee. The visit is also a notable one for the show itself, as this will be College GameDay's third football trip to Iowa City.

The announcement immediately sent Iowa fans into a frenzy.

Hawkeye insider David Eickholt summed up the excitement simply, writing , "Can't get much bigger than this."

Barstool Iowa kept its reaction shorter, proclaiming , "GOATS HOME."

247Sports' Eliot Clough also felt the energy building, acknowledging , "That's a big one. Caitlin Clark mania is returning back to Iowa City."

Another Clark supporter pointed out that the timing could hardly be better. Nike's three-day Caitlin 1 pop-up block party is running in downtown Iowa City through Saturday, right near the Pentacrest, where GameDay is set up, making her guest-picker appearance feel like a natural fit for a weekend already centered on her.

"I had guessed this and she may have done it even had they won last night. The crossover promotion is just too good with her big shoe event in Iowa City extending thru Saturday," the fan wrote .

"The opportunity to do College Gameday and drop in on her shoe celly is simply too perfect to pass up. Gonna be a zoo there tomorrow and lord do I wish I were there."

Hawkeye Sports columnist Chad Leistikow made clear that Clark's presence takes an already major weekend to another level entirely, commenting, "The weekend in Iowa City just got even bigger."

Another reaction came from former UNCO point guard Molly McGrath, who wrote , "The rumors are true!!!!"

One excited CC fan simply posted , "Omggggggg."

Clark's return carries plenty of meaning for Iowa fans. She led the Hawkeyes to back-to-back national championship games and became one of the biggest stars in college basketball before entering the WNBA.

Iowa announced in 2024 that it would retire Clark's No. 22, and she finished her college career as the NCAA Division I scoring record holder for men's or women's basketball.

Now, she gets to return to the place where that rise began for another major Iowa sporting event.

Clark's visit to Iowa lines up perfectly with Nike's launch of the Caitlin 1. The shoe officially launched Oct. 1 and is being rolled out in roughly 5,000 stores, reportedly giving it the largest retail footprint for a Nike Basketball signature debut.

The Caitlin 1 pop-up block party in downtown Iowa City is also running through Oct. 3.

So while Iowa prepares for one of its biggest football games of the season, Clark has plenty going on around it. The Fever star gets to return to her old college home, soak in the buzz around her first Nike signature shoe, and pick a winner on College GameDay.

And judging by the early reaction, Iowa City is more than ready to have its Hawkeye legend back home.

A su estadística le añadió seis rebotes, siete asistencias y dos recuperaciones. Su único lunar, seis pérdidas. Torrens ya ha inscrito su nombre en los libros de récords de la Liga U, que acaba de comenzar su segunda edición. Los anteriores topes de anotación y valoración estaban en poder de Egor Amosov, jugador del Real Madrid que este verano se ha marchado a la NCAA y jugará en UConn. El talento ruso hizo 42 puntos y 46 de valoración en un partido ante el Valencia Basket disputados a finales de octubre del año pasado.

articles.title: ‘Lethal Shooter’ Chris Matthews Still Wants to Train Barack Obama
articles.summary: Chris “Lethal Shooter” Matthews has worked with NBA stars and recognizable names far outside professional basketball, but one famous hoops enthusiast remains...
articles.body:
Chris "Lethal Shooter" Matthews has worked with NBA stars and recognizable names far outside professional basketball, but one famous hoops enthusiast remains on his wish list, former President Barack Obama.

Matthews named Obama during a new appearance on TMZ Sports while running through the people he would still like to get into the gym. "Barack Obama, come on," he said as the conversation moved through his dream clients.

The list extended well beyond the former president, spanning sports, movies, music and television. Matthews also floated Mike Tyson, Samuel L. Jackson, Stevie Wonder, Oprah Winfrey and Denzel Washington, although he did not say that training sessions had been arranged with any of them.

Obama's name was not a spontaneous addition to the latest interview. Matthews had already identified him as a dream client earlier in 2026.

Obama Has Been on Matthews' Wish List Since April

In an April interview with DC News Now , Matthews was asked who he still wanted to work with after building his basketball-training brand. The outlet's report listed Obama, Denzel Washington and Magic Johnson as the three names he gave at the time.

There is an obvious basketball connection behind Matthews' interest in Obama. The archived Obama White House site records that the White House tennis court was adapted early in his presidency so it could also host full-court basketball, and Michelle Obama said publicly in 2010 that basketball was his favorite sport and that he would play it every day if he could.

Matthews Already Works Across the NBA and Entertainment

TMZ notes that he has trained Justin Bieber and Michael B. Jordan in addition to NBA players including Jaylen Brown and Anthony Davis. His basketball resume extends much further than those examples.

Matthews has spent years working as a shooting specialist with professional players, tailoring mechanics to individual bodies, roles and shot profiles instead of teaching every client the same motion.

His work with Davis was documented by Sports Illustrated during the Lakers' championship era, while Matthews has also discussed his training with Brown in later interviews.

His sessions with actors, musicians and other public figures allow Matthews to package shooting instruction into social-media clips that can reach audiences beyond people who follow NBA skills training.

His Latest Dream List Stretches From Mike Tyson to Oprah

The new TMZ interview showed how broadly Matthews now defines a potential client. He started with Mike Tyson and Samuel L. Jackson before making one of the more unusual pitches of the conversation for Stevie Wonder.

Matthews argued that Wonder's musical sense of rhythm and ability to follow sound could translate into learning shooting mechanics. "Trust me, bro. He can make a jump shot," he told TMZ before explaining the connection he saw between musical timing and basketball.

Obama and Oprah Winfrey came next, followed by Washington. The mix effectively spans boxing, acting, music, television and politics rather than staying within the usual pool of athletes.

NBA All-Star Weekend Put His Crossover Coaching on Display

Matthews' ability to move between serious player development and entertainment was particularly visible during 2026 NBA All-Star Weekend in Los Angeles. The NBA listed him as one of the coaches for the Ruffles NBA All-Star Celebrity Game alongside figures including Giannis Antetokounmpo, Mookie Betts, Anthony Anderson and trainer Chris Brickley.

Before the game, the NBA also highlighted Matthews working directly with GloRilla on her jump shot. The league posted footage of the rapper getting last-minute shooting tips before she took the court in the Celebrity Game.

articles.title: Gabby Williams refused to be denied in Game 3, guiding the Golden State Valkyries to a first-ever WNBA playoff series win
articles.summary: The Valkyries win a Game 3 thriller, and their first-ever WNBA playoff series, thanks to the heroics of Gabby Williams.
articles.body:
This truth was perfectly illustrated in Game 3 of the first-round WNBA playoff series between the Golden State Valkyries and Dallas Wings.

A 20-0 sprint by Wings, beginning in the second quarter and extending into the third, seemed to have Dallas soaring toward the first-round upset and into the semifinals. Arike Ogunbowale again was the engine, proving she was not out of scoring gas after her playoff-record 45 points in Game 2. Arike dropped 17 points in the first half, on her way to a 30-ball.

Gabby Williams, who dueled Ogunbowale in Game 2, also showed she had more to give.

But first, with the Valkyries down 16 points, Veronica Burton, finally, ended the Golden State scoring drought—and kickstarted the comeback. From there, the Valkyries issued their own 14-4 run to close the third quarter, cutting the margin to five points to begin the fourth.

Williams then went to work, scoring 11 of her 19 points in the final frame, including the go-ahead middie with with less than 90 seconds remaining, to ultimately set up Golden State for the 77-73 Game 3 victory and the franchise's first-ever series win.

Tiffany Hayes, who again stepped up with 18 points from off-the-bench, said of Williams :

Big shot Gabby. She's our dog, she's our leader and she's the one we go to, and she showed you exactly why. We'll do it again and again, and over and over. … That's Gabby f—ing Williams.

Williams expressed her appreciation for her team's belief in her in the biggest moments, sharing postgame :

I wanted someone to believe in me in the league. I never quite got that belief in the W from a staff or teammates. … The fact they trust me to have the ball in my hands, it's not even about making the right shot, just making the right decisions.

Hopefully, that belief will now inspire more heroics from Gabby, as the No. 2-seed Valkyries now will meet the No. 3-seed Las Vegas Aces, a team not only teaming with belief and heroics but intimidation and experience , in the semifinals. Despite their superior seed, Golden State was swept 3-0 by Vegas in the regular season.

While the Wings certainly will rue the missed opportunity, Dallas deserves tons of credit for turning what appeared to be trending toward an uninspiring sweep into a competitive series. That the Wings, led by tandem of Ogunbowale and Paige Bueckers, who had 17 points and six assists in Game 2, conjured such competitiveness without the services of injured contributors Azzi Fudd and Alanna Smith is even more encouraging.

articles.title: Ibon Navarro: "Me he ido de Málaga, pero Málaga nunca se irá de mí"
articles.standfirst: El entrenador vitoriano, ahora en el Estrella Rojam se acuerda del Unicaja desde Serbia
articles.summary: El entrenador vitoriano, ahora en el Estrella Rojam se acuerda del Unicaja desde Serbia
articles.body: Ibon Navarro no se olvida de Málaga. El actual entrenador del Estrella Roja de Belgrado ha repasado sus primeros pasos al frente del conjunto serbio en una entrevista con Arena Sport y ha echado la vista atrás para recordar una etapa que marcó su carrera y también su relación con la ciudad. El técnico vitoriano fue preguntado por el famoso cántico del ‘plan’, convertido en una de las señas de identidad de su etapa en el Unicaja. Navarro explicó que todo comenzó de una manera mucho más sencilla de lo que terminó siendo. Durante la final de la Copa del Rey disputada en Badalona en 2023, un aficionado malagueño situado detrás de su banquillo comenzó a repetir constantemente aquello de «¿cuál es el plan?». Con el tiempo, la grada terminó poniéndole música y convirtiéndolo en cántico. «No sé cuál es el plan, pero lo que tuviese fue muy bien», recordó entre risas el entrenador, que dejó una huella profunda durante sus años en el banquillo del Unicaja. Su etapa en Málaga estuvo acompañada además por una de las épocas más exitosas de la historia del club. Bajo su dirección, el equipo conquistó dos Copas del Rey, dos Basketball Champions League, dos Copas Intercontinentales FIBA y una Supercopa Endesa. Un ciclo que también permitió recuperar el ambiente en el Martín Carpena y devolver la ilusión a una afición que volvió a vivir al baloncesto de una manera especial. Navarro mantiene intacto ese vínculo pese a haber emprendido una nueva aventura en Serbia. «Yo me he ido de Málaga, pero Málaga nunca se irá de mí. Ha sido una etapa muy bonita para mí en lo personal y en lo profesional», reconoció durante la entrevista. Ahora su presente está en Belgrado. El Estrella Roja ha comenzado la Euroliga con una victoria y dos derrotas, todas ellas disputadas como local. Los serbios cayeron ante Zalgiris y Hapoel Tel Aviv antes de estrenarse con triunfo frente al Anadolu Efes (77-72), en un encuentro en el que Chima Moneke fue el máximo anotador del equipo con 18 puntos.

articles.title: JJ Redick: Matisse Thybulle 'is such a unique player'
articles.summary: Lakers coach JJ Redick gave newcomer Matisse Thybulle lots of praise while pointing out one special ability he has.
articles.body:
After lacking functional depth at the wing position for the last few years, the Los Angeles Lakers suddenly find themselves awash in wings and forwards who can, or at least could, significantly contribute this season. Ziaire Williams and Matisse Thybulle are new to the team as solid wings, while second-year man Adou Thiero could make a jump and there could still be a little hope for Jake LaRavia and Jarred Vanderbilt.

Of the five, Thybulle is arguably the most proven player. He's entering his eighth NBA season, and he has always been an effective defender, especially in terms of making plays on the ball, and he has also developed into an excellent 3-point shooter.

Guard Austin Reaves gave a shout-out to Thybulle when he talked about how impressive and tough Thybulle and Williams have been on defense during training camp this week. Coach JJ Redick gave Thybulle some further praise, especially when it comes to the defensive end, via Benjamin Royer of the Southern California News Group .

"Matisse is such a unique player; he just really is," Redick said. "I think our guys, hopefully, at some point this season, will pick up on the fact that if he's in the passing lane, you shouldn't pass the ball over there because he's probably going to steal it."

Thybulle, who is 29 years of age, averaged two steals in just 16 minutes a game while shooting 39.8% from 3-point range last season. He has always been a spark plug, but the concern with him has been his durability.

He played in 30 games last season after appearing in 15 games during the 2024-25 campaign. On the other hand, he appeared in at least 65 games during each of his first five seasons in the NBA.

As long as he remains relatively healthy this season, Thybulle should harass opposing teams on the regular, whether he's starting or coming off the bench.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham's Fever Future Updated by GM After Elimination from WNBA Playoff Bracket
articles.summary: On the heels of a first-round playoff exit, the Indiana Fever have many notable impending free agents to decide if they want to retain as they look to take the next step in their development.
articles.body:
On the heels of a first-round playoff exit, the Indiana Fever have many notable impending free agents to decide if they want to retain as they look to take the next step in their development.

Fever general manager Amber Cox told reporters on Saturday that Sophie Cunningham, who is among that group of free agents, is someone they plan to have talks with about bringing back.

Cunningham spent the past two seasons with Indiana after being acquired in a trade with the Phoenix Mercury. She has been a solid offensive contributor playing primarily off the bench, shooting 42.4 percent from three on 3.8 attempts per game in 73 appearances for the Fever.

Defense is an area where Cunningham and the Fever have struggled recently. Her 113.7 defensive rating ranked among the bottom 20 for all qualified players during the 2026 season.

Indiana finished ninth in defensive rating and 11th in points allowed per game out of 15 teams in the regular season.

In addition to Cunningham, Kelsey Mitchell is also set to become a free agent and seems likely to earn a max contract after a historic scoring season . Caitlin Clark is also eligible for an extension.

The Fever have $3.6 million in cap space with seven players currently under contract for 2027. This is going to be a crucial offseason as the team continues to build around Clark.

Cunningham has proven to be a solid fit with this group, but the Fever's financial outlook and her shooting ability figures to make her a sought-after player that at least opens the door for her potential departure.

The WNBA's free-agent negotiating period is set to begin on February 4.

articles.title: Un escándalo inadvertido: un jugador de los Wizards reconoce el 'tanking' para hacerse con el número 1 del draft
articles.standfirst: Bub Carrington se sincera sobre la manida estrategia que se usa en la NBA, aunque parece que en este caso no será sancionada
articles.summary: Bub Carrington se sincera sobre la manida estrategia que se usa en la NBA, aunque parece que en este caso no será sancionada
articles.body: Llega un momento cada temporada -si no durante toda ella- que algunos equipos de la NBA no ofrecen su mejor versión con la pretensión de perder partidos, quedar lo más abajo posible de la clasificación y tener más opciones de elegir en los primeros puestos del draft a los mejores jóvenes que vienen. El 'tanking', tan evidente como difícil de demostrar. Sin embargo, hay veces que a alguien se le calienta la boca y desvela lo que estaba ahí a ojos de todos pero nadie se atrevía a afrontar. Le ha pasado a Bub Carrington, jugador de los Wizards, que el curso pasado fue el peor equipo de la NBA con un balance de 17-65. El joven de 21 años ha reconocido que hicieron todo lo posible por perder pensando en hacerse en el draft con el prometedor AJ Dybantsa, como así terminó siendo. “Todos nos hemos visto frenados, en cierto modo, simplemente porque estábamos tratando de atrapar a AJ Dybantsa. Eso no es ningún secreto. Pero ahora, no. Nadie tiene esposas. Todos están libres de ataduras”, ha dicho un Carrington que ve al equipo aspirando a las series por el título: "Si a eso le sumamos el cuerpo técnico y los veteranos, tenemos un equipo de playoffs. Eso va a suceder. Si no ahora, cuando sea". Las palabras de Carrington darían para una investigación de la NBA, que en los últimos tiempos se ha mostrada muy preocupada por el 'tanking', ha pensado en medidas para combatirlo y ha sancionado a algunas franquicias. Los Mavericks recibieron una multa de 750.000 dólares en 2023 después de reservar jugadores en los dos últimos encuentros. En febrero de este años, los Jazz tuvieron que pagar 500.000 dólares por dejar en el banquillo a jugadores clave de forma deliberada. Y a los Pacers les costó 100.000 dólares falsear la disponibilidad de sus jugadores para un partido. Sin embargo, el periodista Sam Amick, de 'The Athletic', afirma que, pese a la confesión de Carrington, los Wizards van a salir indemnes de este caso. "Según una fuente, la NBA no sancionará al base de los Wizards ni al equipo por sus comentarios sinceros sobre la estrategia de perder a propósito”, ha escrito.

articles.title: LeBron James Says 'It's Been Great' Building Chemistry with Joel Embiid at 76ers Camp
articles.summary: Amid outside questions about how quickly the new-look Philadelphia 76ers will adapt to playing with each other, LeBron James is apparently having a breeze working with Joel Embiid.
articles.body:
Amid outside questions about how quickly the new-look Philadelphia 76ers will adapt to playing with each other, LeBron James is apparently having a breeze working with Joel Embiid.

Speaking to reporters after Saturday's Blue and White scrimmage, James said "it's been great" building chemistry with Embiid because of their experience as teammates with the United States during the 2024 Olympics.

The 2024 Olympics marked Embiid's first time playing in the Summer Games. He has citizenship in both the United States and France, opting to play for the former in part because of his comfort level with players on Team USA's roster.

Saturday marked the first game action for the Sixers after adding James and Jaylen Brown in the offseason. Things seemed to be working well for the new group.

James, in particular, showcased all of the things that have made him great for the previous 23 seasons, including feeding Embiid on a three-pointer.

After the scrimmage wrapped up, James described Saturday as a "great first step" for the club and a chance to show Philadelphia fans what they have been working on behind the scenes this summer.

Sixers head coach Nick Nurse has the task of making all of these pieces fit together, but it's a good position to be in when the players are James, Brown, Embiid, Tyrese Maxey and VJ Edgecombe.

This is the most-anticipated 76ers season in years, as evidenced by the fact more than 10,000 fans were expected to attend Saturday's scrimmage at Xfinity Mobile Arena.

There's still a long way to go before we know if this group can live up to the hype, but the early returns at least suggest this could be a team that is capable of challenging the New York Knicks as the one to beat in the Eastern Conference.

The next step for the Sixers will be their preseason opener on Monday when they host the Knicks.

articles.title: Fever GM Says 'Attacks on Our Fanbase Have No Basis In Reality, and They Need to Stop'
articles.summary: Following their elimination from the WNBA playoffs, Indiana Fever general manager Amber Cox called for "attacks" against the Fever's fanbase to stop.
articles.body:
Following their elimination from the WNBA playoffs, Indiana Fever general manager Amber Cox called for "attacks" against the Fever's fanbase to stop.

Speaking to reporters on Saturday, Cox read a written statement regarding the narrative surrounding Fever fans, saying, "The attacks on our fanbase have no basis in reality, and they need to stop, especially with members of the media. ... I'm talking about media who have never been to a game at Gainbridge Fieldhouse."

Cox continued by noting that no actions by Fever fans this season rose to the level of violating the WNBA's fan code of conduct.

"Every organization in the league, every organization throughout professional sports, all the way down to youth rec leagues, have to deal with occasional bad behavior from spectators," Cox said. "And anyone who crosses the line in an arena or online needs to be held accountable. Like I want to be really clear about that. There is a line, and people need to be held accountable if they cross it.

"But here's the fact: We did not have one fan pointed out by a player who violated the WNBA code of conduct this season. Not one fan was removed from a game. ... Our fans love this team. They're going to cheer, they're going to boo, and sometimes they might point. It's a home-court advantage for a reason, and it's the same for the Pacers. And all of that is within the code of conduct."

Current Las Vegas Aces and former Fever forward Brianna Turner vehemently disagreed with Cox's statement in a post on X:

The Fever fanbase became a huge talking point during Indiana's first-round playoff series against the Las Vegas Aces.

During Game 2, Aces superstar A'ja Wilson stepped past the baseline and approached a Fever fan who was pointing at her:

Wilson was assessed a technical foul, and although the fan was initially escorted away from their seat, they were allowed to return and it was determined that no code of conduct violation occurred.

Per ESPN's Kareem Copeland , it wasn't the first run-in between Fever fans and an Aces player, as two fans were taken away from their courtside seats after heckling Jackie Young during an August game.

The fans were not ejected, though, and they too avoided a violation of the code of conduct.

The third-seeded Aces eliminated the sixth-seeded Fever in the first round of the playoffs on Thursday, beating Indiana 94-83 in Game 3.
